title: Rotation playback and deterministic audit export for tenant KMS/HSM keys
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Purpose: Provide a deterministic, replayable export of tenant key rotation history and the cryptographic material required to prove past encryption state to auditors and regulators. The feature surfaces a 'rotation playback' capability that can reconstruct the set of wrapped CEKs (customer-encryption-keys), associated wrapping key versions, and signed rotation metadata for any tenant across a given time window. Scope: - Rotation event ledger (append-only) with canonical ordering and signed snapshots. - Export formats: NDJSON (canonical fields) and CSV (regulator-ready). - Deterministic canonicalization rules (UTC timestamps, lexical ordering for multi-key events). - HSM attestation bindings: include HSM-signed rotation receipts where available. Out of scope for this ticket: UI work in Console (will be a follow-up), on-prem install packaging adjustments (handled by Private team separately).
acceptance_criteria: 1) API endpoint GET /tenants/{id}/rotations?start=..&end=.. returns NDJSON with canonical ordering and SHA256 checksum header. 2) Export bundle contains HSM attestation blobs when tenant is using HSM-backed keys. 3) Replay harness can deterministically rebuild previous CEK wrapping tree and validate hashes against stored ledger snapshots. 4) End-to-end tests simulate a 3-rotation sequence and verify exported bundle matches the replay output. 5) Export artifacts are retained for 90 days (configurable) and access is audited.
design_summary: Store rotation events as append-only records in the rotation-ledger service (new small service). Each event includes: tenant_id, key_id, key_version, wrapped_key_blob, wrapping_key_id, wrapping_key_version, timestamp, event_id, and signer_signature. Periodic signed snapshots (Merkle root + HSM signature where available) are produced to allow efficient integrity verification. Canonical serialization uses RFC3339 timestamps and sorted arrays for stable ordering. Exports assemble events in canonical order and produce a deterministic bundle with accompanying manifest (bundle_manifest.ndjson) and bundle_checksum.sha256.
implementation_notes: - Add rotation-ledger service with write API used by KMS/HSM rotation worker. - Extend existing KMS adapter to pass HSM-signed receipts into ledger when available. - Implement 'rotation-playback' module that consumes ledger events and reconstructs wrapping tree. - Export worker will run on-demand and as scheduled job for compliance retention. - Use V1 export contract: fields must be stable; any future schema changes require versioned manifest. - Store export bundles in a restricted S3 bucket with tenant-scoped prefix and strict ACLs.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary tenants): enable rotation-ledger for 5 non-prod tenants and generate exports for 30 days. Stage 2 (internal): enable for Redwood internal tenants and run audits with Compliance team. Stage 3 (customer opt-in): expose export API to selected enterprise customers behind feature flag. Stage 4: general availability with Console links and RBAC controls. Rollbacks: ledger writes are append-only; to deactivate, stop writing new events and flag tenant as 'rotation-export-disabled'; existing exports remain retrievable.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonical serialization and checksum computation. Integration tests: simulate KM S/HSM rotation sequence (create -> rotate -> rotate) using test HSM-stub to generate signatures; validate replay output equals export bundle. Fuzz tests for ordering boundary conditions (concurrent rotations). DR test: export and replay for a 6-month synthetic rotation history to assert performance and memory bounds.
monitoring: Metrics: rotation_ledger_writes_total, rotation_ledger_snapshot_latency_ms, export_generation_duration_seconds, export_success_total, export_failure_total. Alerts: export_failure_total > 5 for 10m (P1), ledger_snapshot_latency > 5s (P2). Dashboards: per-tenant rotation throughput and export size histogram.
decisions: 1) Use append-only rotation ledger (event-sourced) for auditability instead of updating existing key metadata. 2) Canonical export will be NDJSON + checksum; no opaque binary blobs. 3) HSM attestation blobs are stored but not parsed by the service (passed through verbatim). 4) Exports are immutable and signed with an internal signing key to provide additional verification beyond stored ledger signatures.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Ledger growth could be large for tenants with high churn. Mitigation: implement tiered storage, compact snapshots, and archival to cold storage after retention window. Risk: Exposure of wrapped key blobs during export. Mitigation: exports require scoped RBAC, are logged, and are encrypted in transit and at rest; include an access approval flow for high-risk tenants. Risk: HSM availability during snapshot signing. Mitigation: allow asynchronous signing and mark snapshots as 'unsigned' with clear metadata; require manual reconciliation for regulatory requests.
